sources.paraphrase: Equation (2) divides remaining-day payment demand by liquidity sources: the issue-time payment position, central-bank credit limit and remaining receipts. Section 3.1 forecasts remaining totals; Section 3.3 evaluates forecasted LRI values. Section 4 additionally estimates the ratio’s conditional threshold-exceedance probability using residual bootstrap draws. Thus ratio forecasting is supported; describing only the probability model would omit Section 3.3. These targets concern forward liquidity monitoring and demand/resource uncertainty, rather than the present two-sided absolute sampled-position peak quantile or an executed same-target baseline.
sources.target_symbolic_readback: LRI(i,t,j) = RPD(i,t,j) / [PI(i,t,j) + CL(i,t,j) + RPI(i,t,j)]; risk probability in (14) is Pr[LRI(i,t,j) >= C | I_t]. Symbols are a mathematical readback, not a new estimate.
sources.verdict: Current Section 2 sentence is an accurate concise target classification. Replacing it with threshold-exceedance probabilities is not a necessary correction: that describes Section 4, while Section 3.3 separately forecasts LRI values. No source-backed reason to expand the paper's novelty claim follows.

sources.paraphrase: Section 2 constructs each day's largest final net debit across direct clearers. Section 3(a) also forms time-block maxima, while POT and inverted tail distributions produce extreme exposure levels; the collateral illustration updates estimates monthly. Thus the current cross-participant end-of-day wording is correct, but saying the paper has no temporal maxima would be wrong. It is substantive precedent for extrema-based financial exposure and collateral quantiles. Its cross-sectional daily settlement object differs from a single signed dealer series' two-sided future sampled-position peak with an issue-known floor.
sources.verdict: Current Section 2 sentence is supported. Temporal-block aggregation is an important scope boundary, not a demonstrated error in that concise sentence.
